title: Why RAG? Grounding LLMs in Your Data

scenes.heading: Why RAG? Grounding LLMs in Your Data
scenes.narration: Let's unpack why Retrieval-Augmented Generation exists, and how it stops a language model from confidently making things up.

scenes.heading: The problem RAG solves
items: An LLM only knows its training data
Your private docs were never in the weights
Anything after the cutoff is unknown
So it guesses fluently instead of admitting it
scenes.narration: A language model is a next-token predictor, not a database. It never saw your internal wiki, and it knows nothing after its training cutoff. When you ask anyway, it doesn't say 'I don't have that document' — it fills the gap with a fluent, confident guess. That gap between fluency and factuality is exactly what RAG is built to close.

scenes.heading: Retrieve, then generate
steps: Passages are pasted into the prompt
scenes.narration: RAG splits the work in two. First a retriever finds the passages most relevant to the question. Those passages are dropped straight into the prompt, so the model's job shifts from recalling a fact to reading supplied text and answering from it — a task it's far better at. And because every claim traces back to a passage, the answer can cite its exact source.

scenes.code:
def rag_answer(question):
    passages = retrieve(question, k=3)      # 1) find relevant chunks
    context = "\n\n".join(passages)
    prompt = (
        f"Answer using ONLY the context below.\n\n"
        f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}"
    )
    return llm([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])  # 2) generate from it
scenes.heading: The core RAG loop in code
scenes.narration: Here's the whole idea in eight lines. First we retrieve the top-k passages for the question. Then we build a prompt that instructs the model to answer using only that context, and generate. The 'ONLY the context' instruction is what keeps the model grounded instead of drifting back to its unreliable memory.

scenes.text: RAG grounds answers in retrieved text, cutting hallucination and letting you cite sources — but quality is only as good as retrieval.
scenes.narration: Prefer RAG over fine-tuning whenever knowledge is fresh, private, or must be attributable — the external store updates instantly and preserves provenance. Just remember: a RAG answer is only as good as the passages it retrieved, which is why the rest of the track is about retrieving the right ones.
